transcript:
User: Before you start your pitch — is this one of those AI robots? Be straight with me.
Agent: Yeah, you’re right to ask — I am, I’m Linda, an AI assistant on Jay’s team at Dialux who handles the intro and scheduling so he can focus on the deep-dive calls.  

What made you call in today—was it an ad, a voicemail from Jay, or were you just searching around for options?
User: Great, a robot answering robots. Just get me a human callback, won't schedule anything with software.
Agent: Got it, I hear you — you’d rather have an actual person call you back instead of booking something through me.  

I can flag this for Jay’s team as a callback request; what’s the best time window for a human to ring you back — mornings, afternoons, or late in the day?
User: Afternoons work best. Just make sure it's an actual person who calls, not another robot.
Agent: Got it, afternoons and definitely a real person — no more robots.  

Quick thing so I can get you to the right human: are you mainly calling about missed customer calls, or something else on your phones that’s bugging you?
User: Mainly about missed calls. Just ensure a real person calls me back in the afternoon. No more robots, please.
Agent: Got it, you’re calling mainly about missed calls, and you only want to talk with a real person, in the afternoon — no more robots. I’ll pass that to Jay’s team exactly that way so a human gives you a call back this afternoon; you don’t need to do anything else on your end. Thanks for letting me know what you prefer, we’ll take it from here and have a real person follow up with you.
